v.why: Replacing a removed edge with a conv gains more than replacing an already useful op.
Edge 0 feeds node 1, so replacing a dead edge with a conv gives a large gain, more than replacing a working op.
Replacing a removed edge into the output with a 3x3 conv yields a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
Restoring a removed first edge with any conv gives a large gain.
The upgrade replaces the weakest possible op, so the gain is larger than when replacing a working op.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the final edge to a skip loses learned capacity, which costs more than replacing a weak op.
Swapping a strong conv for a skip loses capacity, unlike swapping a weak op.
Replacing a conv with pooling loses more than replacing a weak op.
Removing the last remaining edge into the output node is far more damaging than removing one of several.
Removing the last non-direct input to node 3 cuts off the learned paths and costs much more.
